why: The brief's mutation 3: the check on a title that begins with Status is gone, so a malformed status prefix (`**Status: shipped.**`, `**Status Nov 12: …**`) shows as the row's title instead of failing loudly.
A failed read logs the error's whole text, which could carry what GitHub sent; the log must name the error only.
The parser collects rows in reverse, so the ranks no longer follow the file's order.
The page never asks for the backlog, so /triage shows only its loading line.
Round 1, major: the triage load stops naming the backlog's source, so production shows no section while the page tests, which pass the prop by hand, stay green.
Round 1, major: the check matches only `Status` in its exact case, so `**status 2026-11-11: …**` shows as the title.
Rounds 3 and 4: leading symbols are not stripped before the check, so `~~Status …~~`, `_Status …_` or a zero-width space shows as the title.
Round 4: HTML tags are not dropped before the check, so `<s>Status 2026-…</s>` shows as the title.
The operator's answer (b), 2026-11-23: statuses are read from every cell. With the columns after the item cell no longer scanned, P1-93's status in the "Start here" column shows as no status.

Answer (b): a status outside the item cell must stand at the start, after a space or after a bold opener. With that check gone, `~~Status …~~` is read as a live status instead of failing loudly. (A status in a code span still fails, on the check of what follows its date.)
Answer (b): the newest status by date wins across cells. Taking the last one found instead shows an older status from a later column.
